sources.title: NGSS 5-ESS1-2: Represent data in graphical displays to reveal patterns of daily changes in length and direction of shadows, day and night, and the seasonal appearance of some stars in the night sky
OpenStax Astronomy 2e, 6.2 Telescopes Today (Earth rotates from west to east)

note.text: The sun lights up Earth, but only one half at a time.
The sun gives off light in every direction. A tiny part of it reaches Earth.

steps.title: Sunlight
steps.instruction: Draw the three arrows of sunlight.

note.text: Sunlight travels across space and lands on the half of Earth facing the sun.

steps.title: Day side
steps.instruction: Trace the half of Earth facing the sun, and the line down the middle.

note.text: On the side facing the sun, it's daytime.

steps.title: Night side
steps.instruction: Trace the other half of Earth, and the middle line again.

note.text: On the side facing away from the sun, it's night.

steps.title: Rotation
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow showing Earth spinning.

note.text: Earth turns on its axis every 24 hours, from west to east. That's why the sun seems to rise and set.

steps.title: Color
steps.instruction: Color the day side and the night side.

options.text: Earth spinning, so each place turns toward the sun and then away
options.feedback: Yes. As Earth rotates, your side of Earth turns into sunlight (day) and then out of it (night).

options.text: The sun moving around Earth every day
options.feedback: It looks that way, but it's Earth that turns. The sun only seems to move.

options.text: The sun switching off at night
options.feedback: The sun always shines. At night, your side of Earth faces away from it.
Clouds don't cause night. Your side of Earth turns away from the sun.

steps.title: Predict
steps.question: It's noon where you live. Is it noon everywhere on Earth?

options.text: No: on the far side of Earth, it's night
options.feedback: Right. Only the half facing the sun has daytime. On the other half, it's night.

options.text: Yes, all of Earth has the same time
options.feedback: Look at the model: half of Earth faces away from the sun, so it's night there.

options.text: Yes, because there's only one sun
options.feedback: There's one sun, but it lights only the half of Earth facing it.
Even in summer, the side facing away from the sun has night.
